adversarial_interpretation: A fresh deterministic-temperature rerun can still differ from ARC-R018 serving; this measures candidate coverage under the frozen protocol, not the unknowable historical unpersisted candidate set.
decision_boundary: On the four prior parseable ARC-R018 failures, candidate-set coverage <50% => generator/representation bottleneck; >=50% with wrong selections => selector/ranking bottleneck.
primary_variable: instrumentation only: persist and exact-score every generated candidate

candidates.rule: Fill interior of each red rectangle with green (3) if it contains a red pixel inside, else fill with yellow (4). Preserve red borders and internal red pixels.

For each red rectangle, if its width is greater than height, fill interior with green (3); if height greater than width, fill with yellow (4); if square, fill with green. Preserve red borders and internal red pixels.

Fill interior of each red rectangle with green (3) if it contains an internal red pixel, else with yellow (4). For rectangles without internal red, use yellow. Preserve red borders and internal red pixels.
Move the red (2) object vertically so its bottom row aligns with the bottom row of the azure (8) object, preserving shape.
Move the red (2) object horizontally so its leftmost column aligns with the leftmost column of the azure (8) object.
Move the red (2) object so its top-left cell aligns with the top-left cell of the azure (8) object.

For each color appearing exactly twice, draw a vertical line through both points. For colors appearing once, draw a vertical line through that point. Then connect the two points of each color with a horizontal line at the row of the lower point, but only if the vertical line passes through that row.

For each color, draw a vertical line through all its occurrences. Then, for each pair of same-colored points, draw a horizontal line at the row of the lower point connecting the vertical lines, but only if that row is between the two points' columns.

For each color, draw a vertical line through all its points. Then, for each color with two points, draw a horizontal line at the row of the lower point, spanning from the leftmost to rightmost column of that color's vertical lines, but only if that row is below the upper point.

Partition grid by the full horizontal and vertical separator lines. Extract the four corner regions, crop each to its bounding box, and arrange them in a 2x2 grid in reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).
Remove the separator lines (row 7 and column 6). Then take the four quadrants, trim all-zero borders, and stack them in a 2x2 layout: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

Split the input at the full horizontal and vertical lines. For each of the four resulting subgrids, crop to the minimal rectangle containing all non-zero cells. Place these crops in a 2x2 grid in the same relative positions.
Map each color by a fixed permutation: 5->1,8->9,6->2,2->6,3->4,9->8,4->3,1->5. Apply to all cells.

Treat non-zero cells as seeds. For each seed, draw a diagonal ray down-left and down-right with its color, and fill the top row with the topmost seed's color repeated between its column and the next seed's column. Overlay all rays and fills.

Use the left column seeds (2,4,8,6,3) and right column seeds (7,7) plus top seeds (9,9). For each seed, extend diagonally down-left and down-right, and also fill the top row between the two 9s with 9s. Overlay all diagonals.

For each non-zero cell, draw a diagonal line of that color down-left and down-right until edge. Also, for the top row, fill between the two 9s with 9s. Then, for each column, fill any zeros with the nearest non-zero color from above or below, preferring above.
